detail.title: 1. The rest of the medical part: a whole version a round, or a line or two for each section?
detail.where: Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue, P1
detail.question:
Nine sections of the medical part read AI in the first batch and haven't been fixed: Call medics for, Who to Contact, Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue (these two paragraphs), My Brain Feels Damaged, Active Seizure's first part, MDMA's jaw tension, Chest Pain, Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion's charcoal and poison control paragraphs, and Serotonin Syndrome. How each option would go:

A: as now: one teaching card a round, and I carry what you do to the others and test them. Pro: you write one section a round. Con: my carries of your two medical versions read AI in all eight tries, so so far only the section you write turns Human.

B (my pick): next round, a short box for each of those sections, for a line or two of your own there: what you've seen, what you'd do, or what you think of the standard advice. I build each section around what you write and test it. Pro: the whole part in a round or two, and it's how my fixes went Human in the remedies, where something you wrote was near (Nausea Smoothers, DMSO, the ocean water). Con: untried on clinical text; a section that still reads AI comes back to you as a teaching card.
